title: Error by AI scribe during medical appointment leaves patient devastated

reports.title: Error by AI scribe during medical appointment leaves patient devastated

summary:
Rebecca Green agreed to let an AI scribe transcribe her first urologist appointment, but the tool falsely recorded that she micro-dosed psychedelic mushrooms. She discovered the error after kidney stone surgery in March, when a post-operative letter to her GP repeated the claim, and she worried it could affect her workers' compensation case. After she complained, the urologist apologised, corrected the record, and said she would review how AI was used in her practice. The medical regulator AHPRA said clinicians must always check AI output for accuracy.

A report by Digital Rights Watch found unregulated AI medical scribes can invent symptoms or conditions, sometimes without proper patient consent, including recording the wrong breast in a cancer diagnosis and a false epilepsy history. The Royal Australian College of GPs estimates 40 per cent of GPs regularly use AI scribes, a figure it considers conservative. Australia's Therapeutic Goods Administration is reviewing these tools and will release findings in the coming weeks, with any breaches to be acted upon. Advocacy groups are calling for approved tool lists and stronger safeguards.
